title: Annotatio VI §.VI (2): sacrament integrity if Oral fails in Impious — offer≠receive
pass_a_gloss: Next connected with the Biblical Argument is that SECOND which appeals to the Nature of the Sacrament, whose integrity it thinks does not stand for itself if Oral Eating of Christ’s Body fails somewhere — i.e. in the Impious. Reply (a) Indirectly: Thus neither will integrity stand for the Sacrament if spiritual Eating of Christ’s body fails somewhere, which is confessed to fail in the Impious. (b) Directly: To the Sacrament’s integrity it does not pertain that the whole be received, but it suffices that the whole be offered: Therefore again Oblation and Reception must be distinguished. From the former to the latter the consequence does not hold: For every receptive thing receives not after the mode of the impressing, but after the mode of its own receptivity.
pass_b_english: Second press: if Oral eating fails in the Impious, the sacrament’s integrity fails.
Reply: spiritual eating also fails in them, by confession; and integrity needs the whole offered, not the whole received — Oblation ≠ Reception; the receiver takes after its own receptivity.
source_text: Connectitur proximè cum Biblico Argumento, ALTERUM illud, quod ad Naturam Sacramenti provocat, cujus integritatem sibi non constare opinatur, si Manducatio Corporis Christi Oralis, alicubi, h. e. in impiis, deficiat. Resp. (a) Indirectè: Sic nec constabit Sacramento integritas, si Manducatio spiritualis corporis Christi alicubi deficiat, quam in impiis deficere in confesso est. (b) Directè: Ad Sacramenti integritatem non pertinet, integrum accipi, sed sufficit, integrum offerri: Distinguendum itaque denuo inter Oblationem, & Receptionem. Ad hanc, ab illa, non valet consequentia: Omne enim receptivum recipit, non ad modum imprimentis, sed ad modum receptivitatis suæ.
